mechanism: Bollinger Bands place upper/lower envelopes at k·σ around an SMA so the band width automatically widens when return dispersion rises and contracts when it falls; band width (or upper−lower) is itself a continuous volatility sensor usable on any symbol with standard settings.
data_needed: Close (or chosen applied price), SMA period (default 20), stdev multiplier (default 2; Bollinger suggests 1.9 for period 10 and 2.1 for 50), upper/middle/lower buffers from iBands.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1/Weekly/Daily; GBPUSD H1; Forex/stocks/general; MT5 iBands(20,0,2,PRICE_CLOSE).
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a self-scaling dispersion envelope whose width is the volatility state, not a fixed-percentage channel like Envelopes.
quote: The bands automatically widen when volatility increases and contract when volatility decreases.

mechanism: Classify regime by where price lives relative to BB middle/upper/lower: uptrend when price mostly between MA and upper band (higher highs/lows); downtrend between MA and lower band; sideways when price oscillates through the MA and traverses lower↔upper. Strategy switches with that occupancy regime.
data_needed: Ask/Bid or close vs Middle/Upper/Lower BandArray[0]; optional prior-bar confirmation.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD Weekly/Daily; GBPUSD H1 sideways demos.
why_new_for_mis: Turns BB occupancy into an explicit three-state regime label (trend-up / trend-down / range) rather than only overbought/oversold touches.
quote: during the uptrend prices move between Moving Average and Upper Band most of the time.

mechanism: Sense trend regime from stacked SMA alignment and fresh crosses: one SMA (price>SMA24), two-SMA cross (SMA24 vs SMA50 with prior-bar opposite), or three-SMA cascade (SMA10/24/48 all align and each pair just crossed)—bull when short>mid>long, bear when inverted—used to filter whipsaws of raw price noise.
data_needed: iMA SMA closes for periods 24; 24&50; or 10,24,48; ArraySetAsSeries buffers of length ≥3 for cross detection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5 symbol/_Period; educational SMA crossover EAs.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a multi-horizon MA-stack regime feature with explicit cross-event change detection, not a single lagging average.
quote: If 10 SMA > 24 SMA, 10 SMA > 48 SMA, and 24 SMA > 48 SMA: the signal will be to buy

mechanism: On a market swing (extremum-to-extremum), mark Fibo correction nodes only in the 38.2%–61.8% band; nodes below 38.2% are weak and above 61.8% risk trend failure. Clusters of nearby nodes form an 'accumulation'; multiple reactions share one focus point—sensor of constructive pullbacks vs trend exhaustion.
data_needed: Swing High/Low (ZigZag or FastZZ); Fibo 38.2/50/61.8; list of reaction lows/highs and focus points; optional Minesweeper wait for 2nd/3rd+ reaction.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex/futures/commodities examples; HTF for fewer reactions, LTF to refine nodes; DiNapoli Levels indicator with Depth=400 pts.
why_new_for_mis: Formalizes Fibonacci corrections as validated reaction nodes plus accumulation clusters inside a narrow band, usable as structure sensors rather than decorative Fibo lines.
quote: Joe DiNapoli advised to work only with nodes found between 38.2% and 61.8%.

mechanism: From last completed swing (A,B,C price and AT,BT,CT time), project price targets at 0.318/0.618/1.0/1.618/2.618 of swing height from C and vertical time targets by the same ratios of (BT−AT) from CT—joint price×time target sensor after ZigZag direction flips.
data_needed: Last three ZigZag pivot prices/times; ObjectCreate HLINE/VLINE at computed Price[] and Time[]; refresh on Refresh==1 direction change.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any MT5 chart; DiNapoli Levels.mq5 with optional audio on ZZ reverse.
why_new_for_mis: Adds synchronized Fibonacci time-axis targets to price extensions, a dual-dimension target sensor uncommon in standard Fibo tools.

mechanism: Shows how to split an EA into indicator modules (MM, SL/TP, trail, signals, filter, breakeven) communicating via CopyBuffer, plus a generator and self-optimizing envelope signal module; software architecture and money-management plumbing, not a new market-state sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: iBands channel-reversal demo EA; Envelope self-opt signal (MA period 10–100, shift 1000–10000 pts).
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read—modular programming / EA assembly guide.
quote: Modular programming is a program development method that involves splitting the program into independent modules.

mechanism: For each currency triangle ordered so smb1≈smb2×smb3, compute PLBuy=((bid2−dev2)*(bid3−dev3)−(ask1+dev1))*tick_value*lot and symmetric PLSell; open only when PL exceeds total three-leg spread+commission cost. The residual PL−spread is a continuous cross-pair parity/mispricing sensor (near-market-neutral).
data_needed: Live Ask/Bid for all three legs; tick value; lots (leg3 lot≈mid price of leg2 × leg1 lot); per-leg spread points×cost; commission input; margin check with CF=1.2.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: All Market Watch Forex triangles (default EURUSD+EURGBP+GBPUSD); night low-liquidity names (TRY/NOK/SEK) noted; tick-level.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a multi-symbol parity-gap liquidity/mispricing feature gated by explicit transaction-cost coverage, not single-pair spread alone.
quote: Instead of entering the market mechanically when ask < bid, we should wait till the difference between them exceeds the spread costs.

mechanism: Harvest ZigZag extrema that continue the prior peak/trough (non-decreasing highs for resistance in downtrend / non-increasing lows for support in uptrend); keep candidate A–B–C lines only if AB/AC and BC/AC ratios pass a Fibo-like fibo threshold, min segment lengths, |C−price|<tolerance, limited AB/BC close-cross counts, and correct slope sign—auto S/R relevance sensor.
data_needed: iCustom ZigZag(ExtDepth,ExtDeviation,ExtBackstep); mass[] of peaks/bottoms; fibo, Min_dist, tolerance, Intersection_ab/bc inputs; OBJ_TREND UpTrend/DownTrend.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: M1 vs H4 ZigZag scale demos; EA tests EURUSD H1 2015–2017 and 13 FX majors 2017; modes from-level / breakdown / all.
why_new_for_mis: Produces objectively filtered, near-price sloping S/R objects with explicit quality criteria instead of subjective hand-drawn levels.
quote: we use the extreme values higher or equal to the previous one during a downtrend (for resistance lines), or lower or equal to the previous one during an uptrend.

mechanism: Build geometric-mean basket currency index from directed pair closes, then histogram = SMA_fast(index)−SMA_slow(index) (MACD-like). Divergence between falling price trendlines and rising histogram (or vice versa) senses weakening/ending of the basket-currency trend; confirmed across most basket pairs.
data_needed: Closes of basket pairs (e.g. EURUSD,EURJPY,EURCHF,EURGBP,EURNZD,EURCAD,EURAUD); InpFastEMA=12, InpSlowEMA=26; index series + MACD histogram.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EUR basket index; EURUSD plus collage of other EUR pairs; also USD/EUR index with channels/Fibo/wedges as secondary patterns.
why_new_for_mis: Applies classical MACD divergence not to a pair but to a synthetic single-currency index, yielding basket-wide trend-change sensing.
quote: the change dynamics of our indicator warns of a trend weakening or coming to an end. Indeed, we can see a trend reversal further on.

mechanism: Run ZigZag on combined basket WPR (−100..+100), bin extrema into 1% intervals, count hits per bin across D1/H4/H1 and all 8 baskets; calibrate overbought ~+60..+70% and oversold ~−60..−70% from empirical extreme density (not the classic single-pair −20/−80).
data_needed: Combined WPR(20) per basket; testIndexZig-Zag1 extreme counts; history depth per TF; trade-count at 70% vs 80% thresholds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUD/EUR/USD/GBP/NZD/CAD/CHF/JPY baskets; D1/H4/H1; EUR table fragment and Pair.zip totals (3793@80%, 7885@70%).
why_new_for_mis: Replaces inherited OB/OS constants with a data-driven extreme-histogram calibration for currency-basket oscillators.
quote: the overbought level is within the range of 60% — 70% in case of overbought and -60% — -70% in case of oversold.

mechanism: Enter sell (buy) of the full currency basket when combined WPR closes back through overbought (oversold) after Point1 ≥+70/+80% (≤−70/−80%) into Point2 in [+60,+50] ([-60,-50]); exit when WPR returns to ~0. Tracks per-trade drawdown and 'positive drawdown' while waiting for indicator exit.
data_needed: Per-pair iWPR(20) averaged with direction remap to [-100,100]; SELL1LIMIT/SELL2FROM/SELL2TO/BUY* inputs; basket pair list + bDirect[].
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USD basket on EURUSD chart (EURUSD,GBPUSD,AUDUSD,NZDUSD,USDCAD,USDCHF,USDJPY); also NZD/AUD/EUR/GBP/CAD/JPY/CHF; H1/H4/D1 from 2016.
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes basket-level OB/OS breakthrough as a multi-leg regime-change signal with explicit pattern geometry and H4 profitability edge vs noisy H1.
quote: A trader receives an entry signal on all currency pairs of a basket if an overbought level is crossed downwards or an oversold one is crossed upwards by the combined WPR after the candle is closed.

mechanism: From OHLCV build digital-filter predictors (ftlm,stlm,rbci,pcci,v.fatl,…), impute outliers, normalize, supervised-discretize vs binary ZigZag Class with WOE/IV (drop IV<0.1); feed raw / WOE / dummy sets into darch DNN (optional SRBM pretrain + fine-tune with dropout/maxout) to predict next-bar trend class—neural regime sensor.
data_needed: Cotir OHLCV; PrepareData/SplitData/CappingData/NormData/DiscretizeData; DTcut raw/woe/dum; darch layers e.g. c(10,16,8,2) tanh/maxout/softmax; pretrain/train/val/test splits.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: M15-style digital-filter series in PartIV.RData (timestamps ~2017); binary Class from ZigZag; OneR baseline ~63–64% acc, DNN ~67–70%.
why_new_for_mis: Pairs information-value feature selection with a pretrained deep net as a trainable sequence/regime classifier over engineered filter states.
quote: WOE describes the relationship of the predictive variable and the binary goal variable. IV measures the strength of these relationships.

mechanism: On combined WPR, require MA(10) cross with both |WPR−MA| after and |prior WPR−prior MA| in [5%,10%] (Delta1/Delta2); reject oversized crosses that exhaust the move. Further block buys if WPR≥+60 and sells if WPR≤−60. Alone unprofitable; as filter on OB/OS breakthrough (WPR>MA for buys / WPR<MA for sells) markedly improves H1 equity.
data_needed: Combined WPR(20)+SMA(10); g_dMinSize=5, g_dMaxSize=10; OB/OS ±60; candle-close timer on H1/H4/D1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USD basket via EURUSD; H1 primary (also H4/D1); Tester_EURUSD_Filter.zip with OB/OS+MA filter.
why_new_for_mis: Adds a quantitative cross-amplitude quality band and OB/OS proximity veto so MA crosses become a calibrated change filter rather than raw lagging signals.
quote: Applying the pattern from this article as a filter yielded positive results! We have obtained a fairly smooth curve having a clear profit increase tendency.

mechanism: Treat Asian/Pacific hours as a session regime where EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDCHF/USDCAD/EURGBP typically flatten; gate Bollinger mean-reversion (sell near upper band, buy near lower) to [time_h_start,time_h_stop] with day-of-week mask and div_signal/div_work tolerance bands around the envelope—session-conditional range regime sensor.
data_needed: Server time hour + day_of_week flags; iBands(period≈11–12, deviation≈2); Ask/Bid vs upper/lower±div_work with div_signal undervaluation; optional work_alt reverse.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/AUDUSD/GBPUSD/NZDUSD/USDCAD/USDCHF M30; night window e.g. 01:00–11:00 MSK; 2017 tests; skip Tuesday in one opt.
why_new_for_mis: Explicitly couples clock-session regime with BB flat mean-reversion, giving MIS a time-of-day flat-state feature for majors.
quote: the night trading generally shows flat movement on such pairs as EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD and EURGBP

mechanism: For JPY pairs that stay active in the Asian session, at a fixed hour place symmetric BuyStop/SellStop order_div points from market with SL/TP and time_to_del; first fill deletes the opposite—senses and harvests a one-sided volatility burst while flat removes both.
data_needed: order_time hour; Ask/Bid; order_div/sl/tp points; ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED expiry; day-of-week enable flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY H1; also GBPJPY/AUDJPY cited; entries ~04:00 or 08:00 MSK; 2015–2017 and 2017 windows.
why_new_for_mis: Session-timed dual-pending burst sensor specialized to Asian JPY volatility, complementary to the flat-regime BB sensor on non-JPY majors.
quote: Its idea is to enter the market at the most volatile moment when a sharp movement is possible in any direction. Two pending orders ... are placed simultaneously at equal distance in opposite directions.

mechanism: Compute combined WPR for base and quote baskets (geometric-mean variant), form distance between them; signal when distance breaks calibrated OB/OS after Point1/Point2 geometry—requires simultaneous strength in one currency and weakness in the other. Enter/exit only the single pair (not whole basket), cutting drawdown vs basket entries.
data_needed: testDistance over two basket WPRs (e.g. EUR vs USD or EUR vs JPY); geometric-mean GetValue; SELL1LIMIT≈50–65, SELL2FROM/TO expanded to raise trade count; exit at ~0.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD,AUDUSD,GBPUSD,NZDUSD,USDCAD,USDCHF,USDJPY; H1 profitable on EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDCHF; H4 scarce; D1 near-zero trades.
why_new_for_mis: Converts dual-currency relative-strength OB/OS into a single-pair change sensor with lower drawdown than full-basket deployment.
quote: The analysis becomes more accurate, because it takes into account the behavior of both currencies of the pair rather than one
